items.title: Goldman Sachs’ calm 2027 forecast comes with a catch
items.summary: Goldman Sachs sees steady growth and cooler prices ahead, but its economists warn the real test may land where many Americans keep their savings.

items.title: Goldman Sachs 2027 Economic Outlook For Investors
items.summary: Goldman Sachs expects cheaper energy to lift global growth in 2027, even as the Fed keeps raising rates into March.

items.title: Goldman Sachs reset S&P 500 price target for 2027
items.summary: Goldman Sachs has a number in mind for the S&P 500 next year, and the bank thinks the recent selloff is part of the reason it gets there.

items.title: Bitcoin Just Crashed Toward $66,000. History Says the Worst May Not Be Over
items.summary: Bitcoin's slide has bruised holders, but three past cycles and a 2022 double bottom suggest the first flush rarely ends the pain. Three catalysts and two price lines will decide whether the old highs come back or the floor drops again.

items.title: AMD Just Beat Nvidia by the Widest Margin Since 1999
items.summary: One chipmaker posted record results and landed marquee cloud customers. Its biggest rival lost its CEO and stumbled again. The week produced a split no one has seen in 27 years, and the aftermath may be messier than the headline suggests.

items.title: Nucor (NUE) Stock Fair Value Edges Higher As Analysts Weigh Growth Against Cost Pressures
items.summary: Price targets on Nucor have shifted, with bullish analysts now pointing to a US$300 to US$345 range, while more cautious views cluster around US$280 to US$296. This split reflects differing emphasis on longer term earnings power and cash generation versus nearer term guidance, cost pressures and policy risk, which feeds directly into how much analysts are prepared to pay for the stock. Read on to see what is driving these views and how to track the next turns in the Nucor narrative. Analyst...

items.title: JPMorgan’s Top Credit Cards Executive Is Leaving the Bank
items.summary: Allison Beer, the CEO of card and connected commerce, “has informed me of her decision to leave the firm for an external opportunity,” JPMorgan Co-President Troy Rohrbaugh said in a memo on Friday.

items.title: Diane Swonk Calls Inflation the Most Regressive Tax. Retirees on Fixed Incomes Feel It First
items.summary: A retiree can't ask for a raise or pick up extra shifts, and the one adjustment they get each year follows someone else's spending. One number in your budget decides how hard inflation hits, and most retirees never calculate it.
